gatingCorrection.defect: run() set resourceAcceptance from verdict===PASS alone, so a diagnostic, partial or relaxed configuration (--only-near-limit, altered ceilings, non-default workload counts) could in principle have carried the flag over a workload that was never the qualification workload.
gatingCorrection.realizedNote: Both recorded runs are FAIL, so resourceAcceptance was false in each and no mislabelled result was ever emitted. The defect was latent.
gatingCorrection.fix: qualificationEligibility() gates the flag on the original ceilings, the default workload counts, one complete sequential and exactly two complete overlapping attempts each with a signed terminal finish and independent byte identity, and no ceiling violation.
gatingCorrection.regression: Focused adapter tests, 12/12, including a near-only configuration with a PASS verdict and zero violations asserted ineligible.
gatingCorrection.wiringNote: Closed: the --locate-peak diagnostic executed the wiring end to end and printed resourceAcceptance=false with the typed reasons VALID_ACCOUNT_ATTEMPTS_SKIPPED, BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_ENABLED, SEQUENTIAL_ATTEMPT_INCOMPLETE, OVERLAPPING_ATTEMPTS_INCOMPLETE, VERDICT_NOT_PASS.

causalScope.established: The near-row/key-limit workload exceeds the 96 MiB ceiling in every run of it, including the --only-near-limit control, so the preceding sequential and overlapping traversals are not required to produce it.
notEstablished: That a single row alone is sufficient or causal — the control inserts BOTH a 1,200,024-byte key row and a 1,400,018-byte value row.

That setup or accumulation effects are excluded — the control still runs calibration, the complete fixture build including the old-route refusal, and the full 42-chunk/640-row account traversal in the same isolate.
That no collection occurs — no forced GC does not mean no GC; these runs observe neither collections nor their absence.
Any attribution of the peak to a specific request — the meter samples on a 5 ms timer with no request correlation.
causalScope.notProposed: Shrinking the supported row or history limits. Currently supported records stay supported; any protocol or limit change is a separate review.

workloadMapping.reusedOldFixture: test/r1-resource-fixture.cjs populate() at targetBytes = C.LIMITS.payload — the identical construction the old /reconcile experiment measured.
workloadMapping.oldSemantics: One request materialized the COMPLETE history as a single 1048576-byte signed payload, transported as 32 fixed pages; one extra byte was a typed 413.
workloadMapping.newSemantics: /reconcile/rows selects rows AT a checked cut, bounded per chunk by 32 rows and 262144 stored bytes, cursor-chained to a signed terminal finish. There is no whole-history cap.
workloadMapping.extension: The same account was then GROWN through the real bridge admit path by 24 large and 100 small valid facts, so the complete inventory exceeds the old transport cap. Nothing was shrunk.
workloadMapping.independentOracle: Direct D1 read through the real storage codec plus validateRetained(); the digest is computed from stored rows, never from route output.

method.platform: Linux /proc owned workerd user+kernel ticks; process-wide inclusive measurement
method.cpu: owned workerd process user+kernel delta covering full response; includes competing D1/isolate/inspector work; conservative accounting guard required, never wall-time CPU substitution
method.memory: maximum observed simultaneous totalSize + embedderHeapUsedSize + backingStorageSize; no usedSize double count; native allocations outside these reported categories unmeasured
method.overlap: per-request windows include competing work; whole-attempt delta is reported separately, never sum overlapping windows

limitations: CPU is the owned workerd process user+kernel delta, inclusive of D1, inspector and overlapping requests.
Memory is the maximum observed simultaneous inspector allocation vector, not a universal native-memory bound.
Sampling can miss a peak; these fields do not cover every native allocation.
Local observations do not establish remote provider performance, spending limits, T1, K1 or P1.
A rows-v3 server result is not client memory, staged-profile validation, atomic activation, current permission, phone fit or private recovery.
The independent byte-identity oracle materializes the inventory in the Node harness, outside the measured isolate; it does not enter the memory metric.
The old-profile extra-byte refusal is recorded as an OLD-PROFILE requirement only; rows-v3 has no corresponding whole-history cap and none is asserted for it.

peakLocationDiagnostic.doesNotReplace: the original qualification evidence recorded above; boundary observations add samples and inspector round-trips inside the measured window and can only RAISE the observed peak, so these numbers are not comparable with the uninstrumented runs.
peakLocationDiagnostic.boundaryObservation: DIAGNOSTIC peak-localization run: labelled observations at every request edge. Extra samples and inspector round-trips inside the measured window can only RAISE the observed peak. Not comparable with, and never a replacement for, the original qualification evidence.

peakLocation.limitation: Samples carry order only, never timestamps, so interval DURATION is unknown. Boundary observations add inspector round-trips and extra samples inside the measured window and can only RAISE the observed peak; this run is not comparable with an uninstrumented qualification run.

findings.peakAttributedTo: WITHIN the request near-limit-chunk-15 — an ORDINARY chunk (2 rows, 132,430 row-value bytes, 178,947 response bytes), not an extreme-row chunk.
findings.stepChangesAt: near-limit-chunk-5 (generic extreme KEY row, 1,200,045 B -> 3,202,414 B response): 23.5 MB -> 79,472,936 B; near-limit-chunk-6 (generic extreme VALUE row, 1,400,041 B -> 1,869,075 B response): -> 123,331,466 B, the first ceiling breach.
findings.afterwards: The phase stays in an 89-145 MB band across ordinary ~132 KB chunks and never returns to the pre-extreme ~25 MB baseline.
notEstablished: Causation. observedAllocation includes totalSize, which is committed heap and a high-water quantity; a sustained band after chunk-6 is equally consistent with committed heap not being returned as with fresh allocation per later chunk. At the peak, usedSize 53,069,736 was well under half of totalSize 119,889,920.
Whether collection occurred. No forced GC was used and none is inferred either way.
Interval duration or in-interval timing. Samples carry order only, never timestamps.
The 1,050 ms guarded CPU on near-limit-chunk-6 as a CPU finding: uninstrumented runs measured 700 ms and 1,000 ms maxima, so this may be observation overhead.
findings.codeBackedLeadByReadingOnly: On the large-row response path the same bytes are materialized repeatedly and concurrently: codec.open decrypted buffer + plaintext string; C.encode64 TextEncoder copy + base64 string (4/3 inflation); rows() validation decodes that base64 back to a fresh Uint8Array and C.text()s it; hash(batch) JSON-encodes the row array and re-bytes() it; sign() encodes the whole page including rows; page() re-validates and decodes every row again; parseResponse(C.encode(result)) encodes and re-parses the entire result; worker reply() JSON.stringifies it once more. NOT MEASURED — offered as where to look, not as a diagnosis.
findings.nextAction: Count which of those materializations are live simultaneously on the two named requests, and reduce them. No whole-history or row-limit reduction is proposed; any protocol or limit change is a separate review under root ownership.
